titular: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO and the stock falls 4.34%
resum: New development: Huang has left Nvidia's management and board with immediate effect, and chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. The stock closed Thursday down 4.34%, and the company reports results on 17 November.
per_que_importa: Nvidia is one of the biggest companies in the world and carries a lot of weight in index funds and many pension plans, so its stumble shows up in the savings of people who don't own a single share directly.
xifra_text: drop in Nvidia's share price on Thursday

titular: The 10-year US Treasury yield climbs back above 5.1% and Wall Street slips 0.35%
resum: When the bond market reopened after the Veterans Day holiday, the 10-year yield rose to 5.125%, while the presidents of the San Francisco and Cleveland Fed, Daly and Hammack, acknowledged that more rate hikes will be needed, albeit gradually. The S&P 500 closed down 0.35%.
per_que_importa: When US government debt pays more, borrowing gets more expensive worldwide: mortgages, business loans and also government borrowing, including Spain's.
xifra_text: yield on the 10-year US Treasury bond

titular: Telefónica returns to profit, earning €464m through September
resum: The Spanish telecoms group made a profit of €464 million between January and September, compared with a loss of €1,080 million a year earlier caused by the sale of its Latin American subsidiaries. Even so, it has cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast to 1–1.5% and is keeping its dividend at €0.15 per share.
per_que_importa: Telefónica has one of the largest bases of small shareholders in Spain and is a major employer; its results weigh on the Ibex and on many Spanish savings funds.

titular: The Ibex falls 0.31% and slips back below 20,000 points
resum: The Spanish stock market closed Thursday at 19,965.5 points (−0.31%), dragged down by the Nvidia effect and the round of earnings reports. Naturgy (+2.47%) was the biggest gainer, while Indra (−2.48%) and Santander (−1.88%) led the losses; the index is still up 15.36% so far this year.
per_que_importa: The Ibex reflects how the country's biggest companies are doing, and many Spanish pension and investment funds depend on it; one bad day doesn't change the fact that the year is going very well.
xifra_text: change in the Ibex 35 on Thursday

titular: The UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter
resum: According to the UK's statistics office (ONS), British GDP grew 0.7% between July and September, more than the 0.5% of the previous quarter, and 1.9% compared with a year ago. It grew 0.2% in September after a flat August.
per_que_importa: The UK is one of Spanish companies' biggest customers and the top source of tourists to Spain; when its economy does well, British visitors tend to spend more there.
xifra_text: UK GDP growth in the third quarter

titular: Burberry and Munich Re prop up European stocks despite the Nvidia shake-up
resum: Burberry rose nearly 8% after returning to profit for the half-year, with sales of £1.1 billion (+6%), and reinsurer Munich Re raised its 2026 profit target to €6.6 billion. Germany's DAX gained 0.57% and the Euro Stoxx 50 0.09%, while European chipmakers fell.
per_que_importa: It shows that European stock markets depend less on tech than US ones: when chips fall, sectors such as luxury goods or insurance can make up for it in European funds.
xifra_text: Munich Re's new profit target for 2026

titular: Cisco's sales jump 24% on demand for AI equipment
resum: Cisco brought in $18.5 billion in revenue for the quarter, up 24%, and raised its full-year forecast to $74.8–75.8 billion. Applied Materials, which makes chipmaking equipment, also beat expectations with record revenue of $10.41 billion.
per_que_importa: It suggests that, despite the noise around Nvidia, companies are still spending heavily on AI infrastructure, which affects jobs and investment across the whole tech sector.

titular: Brent rises 3.3% after Trump says no deal with Iran is needed
resum: New development: Trump's remarks and attacks on Saudi energy facilities pushed Brent crude to close Thursday at $95.82 a barrel (+3.3%) and WTI at $88.74 (+2.6%). Even so, both are still down around 2.5% for the week.
per_que_importa: Oil prices end up at the petrol pump, in airfares and in the price of many products, and they're one of the reasons inflation isn't coming down.
xifra_text: price of a barrel of Brent at Thursday's close

titular: Chinese giant JD.com takes over MediaMarkt's owner
resum: JD.com has completed its offer for Ceconomy, MediaMarkt's German parent company, securing 59.8% of its shares for €1,335 million. Ceconomy became a subsidiary of the Chinese group on 12 November.
per_que_importa: MediaMarkt has many stores and employees in Spain; a Chinese owner with deep e-commerce experience could change prices, product ranges and the way it sells.
xifra_text: price JD.com paid for 59.8% of Ceconomy

titular: Today: Tokyo rises, Hong Kong falls, and European GDP and US producer prices are due
resum: By midday the Nikkei was up around 0.8% and the Hang Seng was down nearly 0.8%, with Japanese tech stocks buoyed by Anthropic's stock market debut next week. Today brings the first estimate of eurozone GDP for the third quarter (11:00) and US producer prices for October (14:30).
per_que_importa: European GDP shows whether the economies around us are holding up, and US producer prices hint at whether inflation will stay high, which could lead to more interest rate hikes.
